13_marg751: RABANUS. Now Hebron is a city in the tribe of Juda which was once called Arbe, although in the Greek manuscripts it is wrongly given as Arboc, as also in ours, whereas in the Hebrew it is read Arbe, that is, 'four', because Abraham and Isaac and Jacob were buried there, and the great Adam, although some suppose he [was buried] in the place of Calvary. This was once the metropolis of the Philistines and the dwelling of the giants, afterwards a priestly city and [a city] of refuge. It lies on the southern side, about twenty-two miles from Aelia, where the oak of Abraham, which is also the terebinth, which is also Mambre, was shown until the reign of the emperor Constantine, and his mausoleum [is seen] at the present time. And though a church has now been built there by our people, the place of the terebinth is worshipped round about by all the nations with superstition, because under it Abraham received the angels as guests. It was first called Arbe, afterwards Hebron, from one of the sons of Caleb; and it was founded seven years before Tanis, the city of Egypt.
13_marg752: AND ABNER WENT OUT etc. RABANUS. Josephus explains this passage thus: Abner moved forward a very choice army, to engage with the tribe of Juda. For he was angry against those by whom David had been ordained king. Against him came Joab, sent by David, the son of Sarvia his sister; he was set as captain of the host against Abner. With him were his brothers Abisai and Asael and all David's armed men; and coming to a certain spring in the city of Gabaon, he drew up his line for battle. And when Abner said to him that he wished to test which of them had the stronger army, it was agreed between both that they should send twelve men to fight; and when the swords were drawn, David's men, holding the heads of the enemy, pierced their loins and sides with their swords, until all perished as if in one appointed danger. When these fell, the rest of the army also gave way, and Abner's people were beaten. And Joab did not cease to pursue the fleeing, commanding the armed men to hasten and not to slacken in killing. His brothers also fought most readily; among whom Asael was the more renowned, who had such glory in swiftness of foot that he outran even horses in running. He pursued Abner, turning aside to neither side.

13_marg754: NOW ASAEL etc. GREGORY. Asael signifies those whom vehement fury seizes and drives headlong. They are to be avoided the more cautiously in that same onset of fury, the more madly they are carried away. Whence Abner, that is, 'lamp of the father', flees, because the tongue of teachers, which shows forth the heavenly light of God, when it sees anyone's mind carried along the steep places of fury, refrains from returning the darts of words against the angry man, as if unwilling to strike the pursuer. But when the wrathful are mitigated by no consideration, and like Asael do not cease to pursue, it is necessary that those who try to restrain the furious should not rouse themselves to fury, but show whatever there is of calm; and some things they should put forward subtly, by which they may obliquely pierce the mind of the furious man. Whence Abner pierced his pursuer not with the point but with the butt of the spear. For to strike with the point is to oppose with the onset of open rebuke; but to strike with the butt of the spear is to touch the furious man calmly with certain things, and as it were to overcome him by sparing him. And Asael at once falls, because agitated minds, when they both feel themselves spared and yet are touched inwardly, under calm, by the reason of the answers, immediately fall from that to which they had raised themselves. Because, therefore, struck by gentleness they spring back from the onset of their fury, they die as it were without the steel.

13_marg765: RABANUS. The doorkeeper cleanses wheat when the guard of the mind, by discerning, separates virtues from vices; and if she falls asleep, she admits the plotters to the death of her own lord, because when the care of discretion has ceased, it opens the way to the evil spirits to kill the soul. For Isboseth would not have fallen by an unforeseen death if he had not set a woman at the entrance of the house, that is, a soft guard at the approach of the mind. And the man of confusion is he who is not fortified with a strong guard of the mind, because while he thinks he is practising virtues, the vices creeping in kill him unawares. With all strength, therefore, the approach of the mind must be fortified, lest the enemies pierce it through the opening of a neglected thought.

13_marg783: AND DAVID AGAIN GATHERED etc. David [signifies] Christ, the ark signifies the Church. David sought to bring the ark into his city, but, a cause intervening, he turned it aside elsewhere for a time and afterwards fulfilled what he had vowed; because the Lord, appearing in the flesh, preached the gospel to his own nation, but "blindness in part has happened in Israel, until the fulness of the gentiles should come in, and so all Israel should be saved." David gathered thirty thousand chosen men out of Israel, because the Lord established the primitive Church out of Israel, associating to himself not all but the chosen; "for not all that are of Israel are Israelites, but the children of the promission are accounted for the seed." They are called thirty thousand, that is, perfect in the firmness of faith, work and hope. For three, on account of the confession of the Trinity, pertains to faith; ten, on account of the decalogue, to works; a thousand, on account of its perfection, to the hope of eternal life, than which nothing is higher, as no number is greater than a thousand. For if thou sayest ten thousand, or thirty, or even a thousand thousand, thou dost not go beyond the thousand itself in counting, but multiplyest it, either by itself or by leading it more often through smaller numbers. Multiply three, then, by ten, lest "faith without works be dead"; likewise thirty by a thousand, that faith which worketh by charity may hope for its reward nowhere but in heaven. The chosen out of Israel, then, signify 'peoples rightly believing, working and hoping'. And the men of Juda who were with David signify 'the apostles and teachers', clinging as it were more familiarly to Christ's side; attended by these the Lord rejoices to bring the ark, that is, to enlarge the Church and to set it in the hearts of those who had not believed. The ark is set upon a new cart, that the grace of the new Testament may be poured into those renewed in baptism, and "new wine" be entrusted "to new bottles." The ark was indeed first in the house of Aminadab, who was in Gabaa, because the same faith which the preacher of the Church now [proclaims] flourished also before the time of the Lord's incarnation in those who followed the devotion of the patriarchs. For Aminadab, who is interpreted 'my God willing', signifies either 'Abraham the father of faith' or 'Moses the lawgiver', each of whom keeps the ark in Gabaa, because by a lofty example of virtue he fortifies the breasts of believers. Whence Gabaa too is interpreted 'hill', which is a place in the city of Cariathiarim. When the ark was brought out, David and all Israel played before the Lord with various instruments and kinds of musicians, because, as the proclamation of the new grace begins, the Lord invites all to render praises of humility to God the Father, saying: "If any man minister to me, let him follow me"; "to one is given by the Spirit the word of wisdom, to another the word of knowledge, to another divers kinds of tongues" etc. But as the ark advanced with these and such kinds of gifts, that is, as the primitive Church grew, they came to the floor of Nachor, that is, the floor prepared in the Church of the gentiles to be consecrated by the truth of faith, of which it is said: "He will thoroughly cleanse his floor," where the priest who incautiously touched the ark, as if to correct it, soon fell struck by the Lord; because the people of the Jews, while it envies the gentiles, is deprived of the gift of salvation. While it wishes to mix the law with the gospel, it loses the grace of both. He held it because the oxen kicked. For the oxen to kick is for 'the preachers of the gospel' to act more freely concerning the faith, and not to walk according to the custom of the law, but to interpret the sabbaths, new moons, circumcision and victims spiritually. These, as if erring, they tried to correct who, coming down from Judea, taught the brethren: "Except you be circumcised after the manner of Moses, you cannot be saved."

13_marg785: GREGORY. In the history of David, king and prophet, in which he is said to have brought the ark of God, humility is shown approved, pride condemned and rashness punished. For David, who was not ashamed to dance humbly before the ark, soon deserved to receive the promise of the Son of God to be born of his stock; and the wife who despised his humility paid the penalty of perpetual barrenness. The priest also who rashly touched the ark purged the guilt of his daring by an untimely death. Here it is to be considered how greatly he sins who approaches the body of the Lord guilty, if he is punished with death who laid hold of the ark, the figure of the Lord's body, with less veneration than he ought.
13_marg786: Often, because they cannot be understood, the deeds or words of the better displease the worse. But they ought the less rashly to be blamed by them, the less they can be truly grasped. For what is the mind of the just man but the ark of the testament, which is tilted by the kicking oxen, because often even he who rules well, while he is shaken by compassion for his subjects, is moved from love alone to the condescension of dispensation. But in this, which is done by dispensation, the tilting of strength is thought a fall by the unskilled. Whence the subjects also put forth the hand of reproof against it, but by their very rashness they forthwith fail from life. David offers holocausts and peace offerings before the Lord: Christ commends the faith and devotion of the Church to the Father, he who "is at the right hand of God, who also maketh intercession for us"; who, after the example of David, blessing the faithful and humble, feeds them with the food of the saving mystery. He distributes to each one cake of bread, namely of him who "cometh down from heaven, and giveth life to the world"; and one piece of roasted beef, namely of that fatted calf which was slain for the returning son and roasted in the fire of the passion, saying: "My strength is dried up like a potsherd"; and fine flour fried with oil, namely the flesh most pure from the stain of sin, but, for the sake of human salvation, most rich in delights, cooked in the frying pan of the cross. Fittingly one cake of one bread [and] one piece of roasted flesh is given, because there is "one Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God and Father" almighty. Otherwise: the faithful receive these gifts when, many being one bread and one body in Christ, each of them chastises the wantonness of his flesh and brings it into subjection. They cook [it] in the fire of the Spirit, and make the fruits of good works, most rich with the oil of mercy, to seethe with compassion for their neighbour. But on the contrary the daughter of Saul, having entered the king's chamber, gives no fruit of conceived seed, because those who receive the word of God with the ear only await the day of perpetual death without the offspring of good work.

13_marg792: AND MICHOL THE DAUGHTER OF SAUL CAME OUT etc. GREGORY. It is good to consider what great gifts of virtues David had received, and in all these how strong he kept himself by humility. For whom would it not lift up to break the jaws of lions, to tear apart the arms of bears, to be chosen when his elder brothers were passed over, to be anointed to the government of the kingdom when the king was rejected, to lay low with one stone Goliath, feared by all, to bring back the numerous foreskins proposed by the king when the aliens were slain, to receive at length the promised kingdom, and to possess the whole people of Israel without any gainsaying? And yet, when he brings the ark of God back into Jerusalem, as if forgetting that he was set over all, mingled with the people he dances before the ark. And because to dance before the ark had been (as is believed) the custom of the common people, the king whirls himself in the dance in divine service. Behold, he whom the Lord preferred singularly to all makes himself equal to the least beneath the Lord and despises himself by showing himself abject. The power of the kingdom is not called to mind; he does not fear to grow vile by dancing in the eyes of his subjects; he does not acknowledge himself set in honour above the rest before the ark of him who had given the honour. Before God he did weak or the lowest things, that by humility he might make firm those brave things which he had done before men. What others think of these deeds I do not know; I am more amazed at David dancing than fighting. By fighting he subdued the enemy; by dancing before the Lord he conquered himself. When Michol, the daughter of Saul, still mad with the swelling of royal birth, despised him humbled, saying: How glorious was the king today, uncovering himself before the handmaids of his servants, and was naked, as if one of the buffoons, she forthwith heard: I will play before the Lord, who chose me rather than thy father; and a little after: I will both play and make myself meaner than I have done, and I will be humble in my own eyes. As if he should say: I seek to be vile before men, because I seek to keep my nobility before God through humility. There are some who think humbly of themselves, who, placed in honours, weigh themselves as nothing but dust and ashes, but shrink from appearing vile before men, and, against what they think of themselves within, cloak themselves outwardly as it were with a stiff comeliness. And there are some who desire to be seen as vile by men, and despise all that they are by showing themselves cast down, but within themselves swell as if from the very merit of the vileness they have shown, and are the more lifted up in heart the more they press down elation in appearance. Both these wars of elation David detected with great circumspection and overcame with wonderful virtue. For that, thinking humbly of himself within, he does not seek honour outwardly, he intimates by saying: I will play and make myself meaner. And because through showing himself vile outwardly he does not swell inwardly, he adds: and I will be humble in my own eyes; as if he should say: such as I show myself outwardly, such I regard myself inwardly. What then will they do whom learning lifts up, if David, who knew that the Redeemer would come of his flesh and announced his joys by prophesying, nevertheless pressed down in himself the neck of the heart with the strong heel of discretion, saying: and I will be humble in my own eyes?
13_marg793: GLORIOUS etc. David, when he brought the ark over into Jerusalem, was mocked by Michol. 13_marg795: It is plain that the Spirit of prophecy does not always shine upon the minds of the prophets: "For the Spirit breatheth where he will." Which God orders by a dispensation of mercy, because while he gives and withdraws the Spirit of prophecy, he both lifts up the minds of the prophets to the heights and keeps them in humility, that, receiving the Spirit, they may find what they are from God, and again, not having the Spirit of prophecy, they may know what they are of themselves.
13_marg796: He who takes care to correct others ought to be clean of vices in himself, that he may not think on earthly things, that he may not yield to the lowest desires, so that he may see the more clearly what others must flee, the more truly he himself avoids these through knowledge and life. The eye which dust weighs down does not see clearly a blemish in a limb, and hands that hold mud cannot wipe away the filth laid upon [something]. Which, according to the ancient translation, is well said by way of signification to David, labouring in outward wars: "Thou shalt not build me a temple, because thou art a man of blood." He builds the temple of God who gives himself to correcting and instructing the minds of his neighbours. We are the temple of God, who are built up for the true life by his indwelling. Whence: "The temple of God is holy, which you are." But the man of blood is forbidden to build the temple of God, because he who still lies upon carnal acts must needs be ashamed to instruct the minds of his neighbours.

13_marg799: This is truly said of Christ. For the house of Solomon was full of foreign women worshipping false gods and driving Solomon himself to the same. But in Christ these things are fulfilled, who is "of the seed of David according to the flesh." The Jews understand the son of David promised in this place to be Solomon, and still, with wonderful blindness, say that they hope for another. There was indeed another image of the thing to come in Solomon, because he built the temple and had peace according to his name; for Solomon is interpreted 'peaceable'. At the beginning of his reign he was praiseworthy, but he foretold Christ, he did not show him; whence certain things are written of him as though foretold of [Christ] himself, while Scripture paints in him the figure of things to come. For in the Psalm which is entitled with his name many things are said which cannot fit him, but evidently fit Christ: for in Solomon is the figure, in Christ the truth. For it is known within what bounds the kingdom of Solomon was enclosed, whereas there it is read: "He shall rule from sea to sea, and from the river unto the ends of the earth." But Christ took the beginning of his rule from the river, where, baptized by John and pointed out by him, he began to be acknowledged by the disciples, who called him not only master but also Lord. Nor did he begin to reign while his father was still living (which befell none of those kings) for any other reason than that it might appear that he is not the one whom the prophecy foreshows, saying: When thy days shall be fulfilled and thou shalt sleep with thy fathers, I will raise up thy seed after thee etc. For this is the true peaceable one, who is prophesied to be raised up not before, as Solomon was, but after the death of David; who built a house to God not of wood and stones but of men. Whence: "The temple of God is holy, which you are." For the blessing of the Lord upon the seed of David is to be hoped for for ever; whence with most certain hope it is said, so be it, so be it, according to that: "Blessed be the Lord for evermore. So be it. So be it." And the repetition itself is the confirmation of hope. Whence David: "And thou hast spoken also of the house of thy servant for a long time to come." Then he added: "Now begin, and bless the house of thy servant for ever," because then he was to beget a son, from whom his progeny would be reckoned to Christ. Therefore, since according to the Seventy it was said in the words of Nathan: "And the Lord will tell thee that thou shalt build a house for him," afterwards David himself says: "Because thou, O Lord God almighty, God of Israel, hast revealed to the ear of thy servant, saying: I will build thee a house." For this house we build by living well, and God by helping. When the last dedication of this house shall come, that will be fulfilled which was said by Nathan: "And I will appoint a place for my people Israel, and I will plant them, and they shall dwell apart, and shall be troubled no more; and the son of iniquity shall not afflict them any more, as from the beginning, from the days when I appointed judges over my people Israel." For there were judges before there were kings, and the son of iniquity, that is, the foreign enemy, afflicted the people at intervals of time; and periods of peace are found there longer than Solomon had, who reigned forty years. For under the judge Aod, the son of iniquity [having] afflicted the people, there was peace for eighty years. These things, then, were not promised under Solomon, nor did any of those kings reign in such peace that that nation was not troubled. The place of so peaceful and secure a dwelling, then, is eternal, where there will be the true Israel, that is, seeing God.

13_marg813: IS THERE ANY ONE, THINK YOU etc. Behold, David did not forget the oath and covenant which he made with Jonathan, but fulfilled to the son the mercy which he had promised to the father. David also signifies Christ; Jonathan, who is interpreted 'gift of the dove' or 'gift of the Lord', [signifies] 'the grace of the Holy Spirit'. Jonathan, then, had a little son named Miphiboseth, lame of both feet, whom David called to himself, when the predestination and foreknowledge of God chooses for the ministry of God him whom it sees weak in word and deed for pursuing the desires of the world and worldly business; because him whom the world spurns through the pride of elation, God acquires on account of the devotion of humility. For Miphiboseth is interpreted 'shame from the mouth'. For he whose speech and presence the pride of the world despises will, by the gift of God, appear useful for spiritual ministry in the Church. And what does it mean that David, questioning Siba, the servant of Saul, about his stock, found Miphiboseth, but that Christ, sifting the number of the elect, makes those come to him who, despised, have left the world? For Siba is interpreted 'he came out', Machir 'selling' or 'from weakness', Ammiel 'his people God', Lodabar 'he the word'. And so our David, choosing the contemptible things of this world, and the things that are not, that he may bring to nought the things that are, finding them saleable to the world and set in weakness, joins them, made worthy by the word of preaching, to his people, and grants them royal honour among his sons. Whence David also gave the fields of Saul and the services [of Siba] to Miphiboseth, and commanded him to be at his table with his sons; because Christ, who "raiseth up the needy from the dunghill, that he may sit with princes, and hold the throne of glory," taking contemptible persons out of the world, makes them possessors of virtues and refreshes them daily at the table of the Scriptures. And such beget a son who is called Micha, that is, 'who is this?', because they come to the wonder of the people, who, lately despised in the world, appear glorious in the Church.
13_marg814: I WILL SHEW KINDNESS etc. When David fled from the face of Achis king of Geth, he came to Naas king of Ammon, who showed him kindness. And as to what Achis king of Geth said: "Shall this fellow come into my house?" "David therefore went from thence, and fled to the cave of Odollam", it must be understood: from the house of Naas. If it is asked why he returned to Achis, whom he had first fled, it is to be understood that he to whom he returned was the son of him whom he fled; whence in what follows Achis, with whom David was going down to battle, is said to have been the son of Maoch. For he took this patronymic not from his father but from his mother, who was called Maacha.

13_marg815: WHEREFORE HANON TOOK THE SERVANTS OF DAVID etc. These things signify the war of the devil against the Church. For Hanon, that is, 'their grief', signifies 'the devil', who is the ruler of the Ammonites, that is, of the evil spirits, that is, of a people of sorrow, always set in straits, who desires to press men down or straiten them. Hanon, then, shaves half the beard of David's messengers when the devil stains the speech or conduct of certain preachers by corrupting it. He cuts their garments even to the groin when he reveals in the eyes of men the shameful deeds to which he persuades them. These must needs sit in Jericho until their beard grows, lest they be a reproach to others and an anathema to all, that is, until the increase of virtues springs up in them and they are held worthy to be presented to their king. 13_marg819: ISIDORE. 'Well of fulness' or 'seventh well'. And the Church is called 'well of living water', and to this well the name of the number seven is joined in signification of the Holy Spirit, by reason of Pentecost, on which day the Holy Spirit was sent from heaven. To forty-nine, that is, seven times seven, one is added, since unity is commended. Whence: "careful to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace." 13_marg820: Still weighed down by the burden of corruptible flesh, we cannot so live that no delight of sin can strike at us. But it is one thing to be touched unwilling, another consenting. Holy men guard themselves with the more watchful circumspection, the more they disdain to be struck by evil motions even in passing, so that if the heart should by chance desire anything unlawful, the eye, held in by the mastery of discipline, would refuse to see it. For as temptation is often drawn in through the eyes, so sometimes, conceived within, it compels the eyes outwardly to serve it. For very often a thing is looked at with an innocent mind, but in the very sight the soul is pierced with the sword of concupiscence. For David did not look at the wife of Urias of set purpose because he had desired her, but rather desired her because he looked incautiously. By a just weighing of retribution, he who uses the outward eye negligently is blinded in the inward. And often concupiscence already rules within, and the enticed soul demands like a tyrant that the bodily senses serve its uses, and compels the eyes to serve its pleasures, and opens the windows of light to the darkness of blindness. Whence holy men, when they feel themselves struck by evil delight, restrain by the mastery of discipline the very eyes through which the image of beauty enters the mind, lest sight serve as pander to a wicked thought. And if this is ever neglected to be guarded carefully, the uncleanness of thought passes over into act.
13_marg821: Often a thing is a virtue in history [and] a fault in signification, just as sometimes a fault in the deed is a virtue in the writing of prophecy. For who would not detest that David, walking on the roof, desired Bethsabee, the wife of Urias? Whom, returning from battle, he urges to go home and wash his feet; who at once answered, saying: The ark of God is under skins, and shall I rest in my house? Whom David received at his own table and gave him the dishes by which he was to die. David, then, holds the figure of him of whom it is written: "He hath set his tabernacle in the sun." He orders Bethsabee to be brought to him, that is, the law of the letter, joined to the carnal people, to associate to himself by spiritual understanding. For Bethsabee is called 'well of seven', because through the knowledge of the law, by the infusion of spiritual grace, perfect wisdom is ministered to us. And Urias signifies 'the Jewish people', [he] who is interpreted 'my light of God'. For the Jewish people, which is lifted up by the knowledge of the law it received, glories as it were in the light of God. But David took his wife from him and joined her to himself, because the Redeemer, appearing strong of hand, when he made known that the law spoke spiritually of him, by this, that it was held according to the letter, showed it to be estranged from the Jewish people and joined it to himself, because he declared himself to be preached by it. For the Jew holds the law which speaks of his divinity, in whom he disdains to believe. Whence also Urias is sent to Joab with letters by which he is to be killed, because the Jew carries the law by whose conviction he is to die. For when, retaining the commands of the law, he strives to fulfil them, he himself brings the judgment by which he is condemned. What, then, in this deed is more wicked than David? What purer than Urias? But in the mystery, what is holier than David? What more faithless than Urias? Because he through the fault of his life signifies the innocence of prophecy, and this one through the innocence of his life expresses fault in prophecy. 13_marg822: The sins of David and of Peter are set down in Scripture to this end, that the fall of the greater may be a caution to the lesser. Penance and pardon are made known to this end, that the recovery of the lost may be the hope of the perishing. Let no one be proud at David falling from his state; let no one despair at David rising again from his lapse. Wonderfully does Scripture by the same word press down the proud by which it lifts up the humble. For it related one deed, and in a different manner called back the proud to the fear of humility, the humble to the confidence of hope. An inestimable medicine of a new kind, which, applied in the same way, both dries up swellings by pressing and fills up dry places by lifting. It has terrified us by the fall of the greater, but strengthened us by their restoration. So the mercy of the divine dispensation both represses us when proud and props us lest we fall through despair. But perhaps the reader's mind is moved [to ask] why God does not guard from vices those whom he chooses and takes up to the height of spiritual gifts. But many, through the gifts of virtues received, through the grace of good works bestowed, fall into pride, and yet do not know that they have fallen. Against them, then, the ancient enemy, who already rules within, is permitted to rage without, that those who are lifted up in thought may be laid low through the lust of the flesh. And sometimes it is less to fall in corruption of the body than to sin by silent thought from deliberate elation. But because pride is thought less shameful, it is less avoided. Men blush at lust the more because all alike know it to be shameful. Therefore many, falling through or after pride into lust, blush from their open fall at the evil of their hidden fault, and correct the greater, since, laid low in the least, they are more heavily confounded. For they see themselves guilty among the lesser who believed themselves free among the graver. So by the gracious dispensation of the Lord, the evil spirit often drags those let loose from fault to fault, and the more he strikes, the more he loses him whom he had taken, and is overcome by that whereby he is seen to have conquered. It is good to consider with how great favour of mercy God holds us within the fortified bosom of grace. Behold, he who was lifted up by virtue returns to humility through vice. And he who is lifted up by virtues received is wounded not with a sword but with a medicine. For virtue is a medicine, vice a wound. Because, then, we make a wound of the medicine, he makes a medicine of the wound, that he who is struck by virtue may be cured by vice. For we turn the gifts of virtues to the use of vices; he takes up the enticements of vices into the citadel of virtues, and strikes the state of health that he may preserve it, that we who flee the humility of the healer may at least cling to him when we fall. But many, the more they fall in many things, are bound the more tightly; and when the ancient enemy strikes them with one vice so that they fall, he binds them with another lest they rise. Let a man consider, then, with what adversary he wages war, and if he perceives that he has already offended in something, let him at least fear to be dragged from fault into fault, and let the wounds by which he often kills be zealously avoided, because it is very rare that our enemy serves the salvation of the elect even by his wounds. For the Lord often subjects the elect to the tempter to instruct them, as after the enclosures of paradise, after the secrets of the third heaven, lest Paul should be exalted by the greatness of the revelations, there was given him an angel of Satan. But it is arranged by this temptation that those who could have perished lifted up may be saved humbled. By the secret order of dispensation, then, the kindness of God is perfected by that whereby the iniquity of the devil is permitted to rage, because it obeys the nods of heavenly grace by that whereby it exercises the wrath of its own will.

13_marg860: AND THERE WAS [A FAMINE] etc. RABANUS. The famine that came in Israel on account of the Gabaonites signifies 'barrenness of good works' in subjects on account of the negligence of teachers, who do not provide them the food of the word of God while they serve earthly things. The Gabaonites, then, are killed when the pursuit of right conduct and the reformation of penance after a fall is withdrawn from the unwary, namely by heretics or evil spirits. For Gabaon is interpreted 'hill of grief'. The Gabaonites are killed when the slothful, after committing crimes, are deluded by the devil with a vain hope of security, who say: "Let us do evil, that there may come good: whose damnation is just." But Respha, who is interpreted 'course', the daughter of Aia, who is interpreted 'his father', taking haircloth spread it upon the rock etc., because the loving solicitude of the saints, succouring such, gives itself to the rigour of fasting and the urgency of prayers, until it obtains from heaven the mercy of God upon them, restraining wicked men and evil spirits, lest they further corrupt their life by wicked suggestion.
13_marg861: Saying, namely, that Josue had let the Gabaonites live for nothing, and had unjustly taken away their spoil from the children of Israel and Juda. And the cause of this vengeance upon the Gabaonites was Abimelech the priest.

13_marg865: AND THERE WAS A THIRD [BATTLE] etc. RABANUS. Josephus speaks thus of the third battle: After this encounter the Philistines fought again; and when David sent an army against them, Ephan his kinsman showed himself most valiant. For fighting alone against each of the most valiant of the Philistines he slew them, and turned others to flight, of whom also many fell in the battle. But whether he called Ephan Adeodatus, or someone else, is also uncertain.

13_marg867: The four battles of David and his servants against the Philistines signify the battle of Christ, which is carried on at every time of this life in his members against persecutors and spiritual wickednesses. For though the pride of the world or the insolence of the evil spirits rise up against the Church of God, yet every principality of the adversaries gives way and is brought to nothing, as the true David commands and orders the battle of his servants. Whence: "Vain is the salvation of man. Through God we shall do mightily: and he shall bring to nothing them that afflict us."
13_marg868: Because Noemi and Ruth, from whom David sprang, returned to Bethlehem in a time of plenty, and because Ruth was joined to Booz for the sake of bread, that place was called 'house of bread'. Or because Noemi, having returned there with her daughter-in-law, obtained abundance of bread in the house of Booz.
13_marg869: RABANUS. The seventeenth Psalm alone is found in the books of Kings, because it signifies that kingdom where we shall have no adversary. For its title is: "In the day that the Lord delivered him from the hand of all his enemies, and from the hand of Saul." For David signifies him "who was made of the seed of David according to the flesh," who in his body, which is the Church, still suffers enemies. Whence: "Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?" And his body will be wholly delivered when "the enemy death shall be destroyed last," that one may come to the kingdom of God. This psalm cannot fit one person. For first the prophet speaks, giving thanks because he is delivered from grievous danger by divine mercy, here: THE PANGS OF DEATH HAVE SURROUNDED ME etc. Secondly the Church speaks, which before the Lord's coming suffered innumerable calamities, [and] afterwards God, having pity, granted the medicine of the holy incarnation and by the benefit of baptism gathered the Christian people from the whole world, there: GOD WHO HATH GIRDED ME WITH STRENGTH. Thirdly the voice of the Saviour, of wonderful mercy, glides in, where his power is described with most beautiful allusions, there: THE LORD LIVETH, AND MY GOD IS BLESSED. Fourthly, again the words of the catholic Church are brought forth, and with great exultation the gifts granted by the Godhead are praised.
